meta.subject: math
meta.description: Statistics and probability facts: mean, median, mode, probability, standard deviation, sampling, regression

facts.statement: The mean (average) is found by adding all values and dividing by the number of values
The median is the middle value when data is arranged in order; for even-count data, it is the average of the two middle values
The mode is the value that appears most frequently in a data set; a data set can have no mode, one mode, or multiple modes
The range is the difference between the largest and smallest values in a data set
An outlier is a data value that is much higher or lower than most of the data, and it can significantly affect the mean
The median is resistant to outliers, making it a better measure of center for skewed data
For the data set {2, 3, 5, 7, 8}: mean = 25/5 = 5, median = 5, mode = none (all unique)
A weighted average multiplies each value by its weight, sums the products, and divides by the sum of weights
The interquartile range (IQR) = Q3 - Q1, measuring the spread of the middle 50% of data
Q1 (first quartile) is the median of the lower half; Q3 (third quartile) is the median of the upper half
A common rule: outliers are values below Q1 - 1.5 x IQR or above Q3 + 1.5 x IQR
In a symmetric distribution, mean = median = mode; in a skewed distribution, they differ
To find the mean of a frequency table, multiply each value by its frequency, sum the products, and divide by the total frequency
Removing an outlier from a data set affects the mean more than the median

common_errors.wrong: the mean, median, and mode are always the same number
common_errors.correct: Mean, median, and mode can be very different, especially in skewed distributions.

common_errors.wrong: the median is always one of the data values
common_errors.correct: For a data set with an even number of values, the median is the average of the two middle values and may not appear in the data.

common_errors.wrong: every data set has exactly one mode
common_errors.correct: A data set can have no mode (all values unique), one mode, or multiple modes (bimodal, multimodal).

common_errors.wrong: the mean is always the best measure of center
common_errors.correct: For skewed data or data with outliers, the median is often more representative than the mean.

common_errors.wrong: range tells you how spread out all the data is
common_errors.correct: Range only uses the two extreme values. IQR or standard deviation give better measures of spread.

facts.statement: Probability ranges from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain), and can also be expressed as a percentage from 0% to 100%
The probability of an event = number of favorable outcomes / total number of possible outcomes
The probability of flipping heads on a fair coin is 1/2 or 50%
The probability of rolling any specific number on a fair six-sided die is 1/6
The complement of an event has probability: P(not A) = 1 - P(A)
For independent events, P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B)
For mutually exclusive events, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B)
Independent events do not affect each other's probability; dependent events do
The sample space is the set of all possible outcomes: for a coin, {H, T}; for a die, {1,2,3,4,5,6}
Conditional probability: P(A|B) = P(A and B) / P(B), the probability of A given B occurred
The general addition rule: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B)
Expected value = sum of (each outcome x its probability). For a fair die: (1+2+3+4+5+6)/6 = 3.5
Drawing cards without replacement creates dependent events: P(2nd ace | 1st was ace) = 3/51, not 4/52
A standard deck has 52 cards: 4 suits x 13 ranks. P(drawing an ace) = 4/52 = 1/13

common_errors.wrong: if you flip heads 5 times in a row, tails is more likely next
common_errors.correct: Each coin flip is independent. The probability of heads is still 50% regardless of previous flips. This misconception is called the gambler's fallacy.

common_errors.wrong: probability can be negative or greater than 1
common_errors.correct: Probability is always between 0 and 1 (inclusive). Values outside this range are not valid probabilities.

common_errors.wrong: 50-50 chance means the event will happen half the time exactly
common_errors.correct: 50% probability means the event is expected to happen about half the time over many trials, but any individual trial is random.

common_errors.wrong: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) always
common_errors.correct: This only works for mutually exclusive events. Otherwise, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B).

common_errors.wrong: if P(rain) = 30%, it will rain 30% of the day
common_errors.correct: 30% probability means there is a 30% chance of rain occurring at all, not that 30% of the day will have rain.

facts.statement: A bar graph uses bars to compare categories of data; a histogram shows the frequency of data within intervals
A line graph shows how data changes over time by connecting data points with line segments
A pie chart (circle graph) shows parts of a whole as sectors, where all sectors must add up to 100%
A scatter plot uses dots on a coordinate plane to show the relationship between two variables
A box plot (box-and-whisker plot) displays the minimum, first quartile, median, third quartile, and maximum of a data set
A positive correlation means both variables increase together; a negative correlation means one increases as the other decreases
A frequency table lists each value (or interval) and how many times it appears in the data
A dot plot places one dot above a number line for each data value; it shows shape, center, and spread simply
A stem-and-leaf plot uses leading digits as stems and trailing digits as leaves: 32, 35, 37 have stem 3 and leaves 2, 5, 7
A two-way frequency table shows the frequency of data for two categorical variables simultaneously
The line of best fit (trend line) on a scatter plot shows the general direction of the data
A pictograph uses symbols or pictures to represent data, where each symbol stands for a certain number of items
Double bar graphs and double line graphs compare two data sets side by side on the same axis
A circle graph must have all sectors add up to 360 degrees because a full circle is 360 degrees

common_errors.wrong: a bar graph and a histogram are the same thing
common_errors.correct: Bar graphs compare categories with gaps between bars. Histograms show frequency of continuous data in intervals with no gaps between bars.

common_errors.wrong: correlation proves causation
common_errors.correct: Correlation shows a relationship between two variables but does not prove one causes the other. There may be other factors involved.

common_errors.wrong: pie chart sectors can add up to more than 100%
common_errors.correct: All sectors of a pie chart must add up to exactly 100% since they represent parts of a whole.

common_errors.wrong: you can read exact values from a box plot
common_errors.correct: Box plots show the five-number summary and spread, but individual data values are not visible.

facts.statement: Standard deviation measures how spread out data values are from the mean
A small standard deviation means data points are close to the mean; a large standard deviation means they are spread out
Variance is the average of the squared differences from the mean; standard deviation is the square root of variance
In a normal distribution (bell curve), about 68% of data falls within 1 standard deviation of the mean, 95% within 2, and 99.7% within 3
The standard deviation can never be negative because it involves squared differences
A z-score measures how many standard deviations a value is from the mean: z = (x - mean) / standard deviation
A z-score of 0 means the value equals the mean; positive z-scores are above the mean, negative are below
The sample standard deviation uses (n-1) in the denominator (Bessel's correction); the population standard deviation uses n
Adding the same constant to every data value does not change the standard deviation; multiplying by a constant multiplies the standard deviation by that constant's absolute value
A data set where all values are equal has a standard deviation of 0 because there is no spread
About 95% of data in a normal distribution falls within 2 standard deviations of the mean; values beyond 3 standard deviations are very rare

common_errors.wrong: standard deviation can be negative
common_errors.correct: Standard deviation is always non-negative because it is derived from squared differences.

common_errors.wrong: standard deviation tells you the average value
common_errors.correct: Standard deviation measures the spread of data, not the center. The mean tells you the average value.

common_errors.wrong: all data follows a normal distribution
common_errors.correct: Many distributions are skewed or uniform. The normal (bell-curve) distribution is common but not universal.

common_errors.wrong: a z-score of 2 means the value is twice the mean
common_errors.correct: A z-score of 2 means the value is 2 standard deviations above the mean, not twice the mean.

common_errors.wrong: variance and standard deviation are the same thing
common_errors.correct: Variance is the average of squared differences. Standard deviation is the square root of variance and has the same units as the data.

facts.statement: A permutation is an arrangement where order matters; a combination is a selection where order does not matter
n factorial (n!) equals n x (n-1) x (n-2) x ... x 2 x 1; for example, 5! = 120
0! = 1 by definition
The number of permutations of n objects taken r at a time is P(n,r) = n! / (n-r)!
The number of combinations of n objects taken r at a time is C(n,r) = n! / (r!(n-r)!)
The Fundamental Counting Principle: if there are m ways to do one thing and n ways to do another, there are m x n ways to do both
C(n,r) = C(n, n-r): choosing r items to include is the same as choosing n-r items to exclude
The number of ways to arrange n distinct objects in a line is n!
Permutations with repetition: the number of arrangements of n objects where there are n1 alike, n2 alike, etc. = n! / (n1! x n2! x ...)
Pascal's triangle row n gives the values of C(n,0), C(n,1), ..., C(n,n)

common_errors.wrong: combinations and permutations are the same thing
common_errors.correct: In permutations, order matters (ABC is different from CBA). In combinations, order does not matter (ABC is the same as CBA).
By definition, 0! = 1. This is needed for formulas like C(n,0) and C(n,n) to work correctly.

common_errors.wrong: the Fundamental Counting Principle says to add the possibilities
common_errors.correct: The Fundamental Counting Principle multiplies possibilities. If you have 3 shirts and 4 pants, you have 3 x 4 = 12 outfits, not 7.
C(5,2) = 5! / (2! x 3!) = 120 / (2 x 6) = 10. You must divide by both r! and (n-r)!.

facts.statement: A population is the entire group being studied; a sample is a subset selected from the population
A random sample gives every member of the population an equal chance of being selected
Bias occurs when a sampling method systematically favors certain outcomes over others
In an experiment, researchers apply treatments and measure results; in an observational study, they only observe without intervening
A census collects data from every member of the population
Stratified sampling divides the population into subgroups (strata) and samples from each
Convenience sampling (using whoever is easiest to reach) is prone to bias
A larger random sample generally provides more accurate estimates of population parameters
Cluster sampling divides the population into clusters (often geographic), then randomly selects entire clusters to study
Systematic sampling selects every kth member of the population (e.g., every 10th person) after a random starting point
Response bias occurs when participants give inaccurate answers, often due to question wording or social desirability
A control group in an experiment receives no treatment or a placebo, serving as a baseline for comparison
Random assignment in experiments means participants are randomly placed into treatment or control groups, reducing confounding variables
A double-blind study is one where neither the participants nor the researchers know who is in the treatment or control group

common_errors.wrong: a larger sample always eliminates bias
common_errors.correct: A large biased sample is still biased. The sampling method matters more than sample size for reducing bias.

common_errors.wrong: an online poll is a random sample
common_errors.correct: Online polls use voluntary response, which is not random. People who feel strongly are more likely to respond.

common_errors.wrong: observational studies can prove causation
common_errors.correct: Only controlled experiments can establish causation. Observational studies can show correlation but not cause.

common_errors.wrong: a sample of 10 is just as reliable as a sample of 1000
common_errors.correct: Larger random samples produce more precise estimates. A sample of 1000 has a much smaller margin of error than a sample of 10.

common_errors.wrong: if the sample is random, it will perfectly match the population
common_errors.correct: Random samples are subject to sampling variability. They approximate the population but will not match it exactly.

facts.statement: A tree diagram shows all possible outcomes of a sequence of events and helps calculate probabilities of compound events
Theoretical probability is based on reasoning about equally likely outcomes; experimental probability is based on actual data from trials
The law of large numbers states that as the number of trials increases, experimental probability approaches theoretical probability
For two independent events, the probability of both occurring equals the product of their individual probabilities: P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B)
For dependent events, P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B|A), where P(B|A) is the probability of B given A occurred
A Venn diagram can show overlapping events; the intersection represents outcomes in both events
If P(A) = 0.3 and P(B) = 0.5 and they are independent, then P(A and B) = 0.15 and P(A or B) = 0.3 + 0.5 - 0.15 = 0.65
Geometric probability uses lengths, areas, or volumes to find probability: probability = favorable area / total area
A simulation uses random number generators or physical devices to model probability experiments when theoretical calculation is difficult
In a two-way table, joint frequencies show how often two categories co-occur; marginal frequencies show totals for each category
The probability of getting at least one head in n coin flips is 1 - (1/2)^n; for 3 flips, it is 1 - 1/8 = 7/8
With replacement means the item goes back before the next draw (independent); without replacement means it stays out (dependent)

common_errors.wrong: experimental probability always equals theoretical probability
common_errors.correct: Experimental probability varies from trial to trial and only approximates theoretical probability as the number of trials increases.

common_errors.wrong: a tree diagram shows only the most likely outcomes
common_errors.correct: A tree diagram shows ALL possible outcomes of a sequence of events, not just the most likely ones.

common_errors.wrong: P(A or B) always equals P(A) x P(B)
common_errors.correct: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B). The multiplication rule is for P(A and B), not P(A or B).

common_errors.wrong: rolling two dice, the probability of getting a sum of 12 is the same as getting a sum of 7
common_errors.correct: A sum of 12 can only occur one way (6+6), but a sum of 7 can occur six ways (1+6, 2+5, 3+4, 4+3, 5+2, 6+1). P(sum=7) = 6/36, P(sum=12) = 1/36.

common_errors.wrong: if you pick 2 marbles from a bag of 5 red and 3 blue, with replacement and without replacement give the same probability
common_errors.correct: With replacement: P(both red) = 5/8 x 5/8 = 25/64. Without replacement: P(both red) = 5/8 x 4/7 = 20/56 = 5/14. They differ.

facts.statement: Mean absolute deviation (MAD) is the average distance of each data point from the mean: find the mean, find each absolute deviation, then average them
A symmetric distribution has roughly equal values on both sides of the center, like a bell curve
A left-skewed (negatively skewed) distribution has a longer tail on the left side; the mean is typically less than the median
A right-skewed (positively skewed) distribution has a longer tail on the right side; the mean is typically greater than the median
A uniform distribution has all values occurring with approximately equal frequency
A bimodal distribution has two peaks, suggesting two clusters or groups within the data
A gap in a data set is a large space between consecutive values where no data exists
A cluster is a group of data values that are close together, separated from other values by gaps
The shape of a distribution (symmetric, skewed, bimodal) helps determine which measure of center is most appropriate

common_errors.wrong: MAD and standard deviation are the same thing
common_errors.correct: MAD uses absolute deviations; standard deviation uses squared deviations. They measure spread differently and give different values.

common_errors.wrong: in a skewed distribution, the mean is always the best measure of center
common_errors.correct: For skewed data, the median better represents the center because the mean is pulled toward the tail by extreme values.

common_errors.wrong: a bimodal distribution must have exactly two data points
common_errors.correct: Bimodal means two peaks or modes in the distribution, not two data points. The data set can have many values.

common_errors.wrong: removing an outlier is always the right thing to do
common_errors.correct: Outliers should only be removed if there is a clear reason (measurement error, data entry mistake). Some outliers are legitimate data points.

facts.statement: The correlation coefficient r measures the strength and direction of a linear relationship between two variables, ranging from -1 to 1
An r value close to 1 indicates a strong positive linear relationship; close to -1 indicates a strong negative linear relationship; close to 0 indicates weak or no linear relationship
The line of best fit (regression line) minimizes the sum of squared vertical distances (residuals) between the data points and the line
The equation of a regression line is y = mx + b, where m is the slope and b is the y-intercept
Interpolation is predicting within the range of observed data; extrapolation is predicting outside that range and is less reliable
A residual is the difference between an observed value and the predicted value from the regression line: residual = observed - predicted
r-squared (R^2) represents the proportion of variance in the dependent variable explained by the independent variable; r^2 = 0.81 means 81% of variance is explained
A residual plot helps assess whether a linear model is appropriate; a random scatter of residuals suggests linearity; a pattern suggests nonlinearity

common_errors.wrong: an r value of 0.5 means the relationship is 50% strong
common_errors.correct: r = 0.5 indicates a moderate positive correlation. The r-squared value (0.25) indicates 25% of variance is explained by the linear relationship.

common_errors.wrong: the line of best fit must pass through every data point
common_errors.correct: The line of best fit approximates the overall trend. Most points will be above or below the line; only rarely does it pass through actual data points.

common_errors.wrong: a correlation of -0.9 is weaker than a correlation of 0.5
common_errors.correct: Correlation strength is determined by the absolute value. |-0.9| = 0.9 > |0.5| = 0.5, so -0.9 is a stronger (negative) correlation.

common_errors.wrong: extrapolation is just as reliable as interpolation
common_errors.correct: Extrapolation predicts outside the observed data range and is much less reliable. The pattern may not continue beyond the data.

facts.statement: A percentile indicates the value below which a given percentage of observations fall: the 90th percentile means 90% of data falls below that value
The five-number summary consists of minimum, Q1, median, Q3, and maximum
To construct a box plot: draw a box from Q1 to Q3, a line at the median, and whiskers extending to the minimum and maximum (or to 1.5 x IQR from quartiles)
The margin of error gives a range above and below a sample statistic: if a poll shows 52% with margin of error 3%, the true value is likely between 49% and 55%
A confidence interval is a range of values that likely contains the true population parameter, such as a 95% confidence interval
The 50th percentile is the same as the median
When comparing two box plots, compare the medians for center, the IQR for spread, and look for overlap to assess differences
Standard error measures how much a sample statistic (like the mean) is expected to vary from sample to sample; SE = standard deviation / sqrt(n)

common_errors.wrong: the 90th percentile means 90% of the data is above that value
common_errors.correct: The 90th percentile means 90% of the data falls AT OR BELOW that value, and 10% falls above.

common_errors.wrong: a 95% confidence interval means there is a 95% chance the true value is in the interval
common_errors.correct: It means that 95% of such intervals constructed from random samples would contain the true value. Any single interval either contains it or does not.

common_errors.wrong: two box plots that overlap cannot have different medians
common_errors.correct: Box plots can overlap substantially and still have different medians. The overlap relates to spread, not just center.

common_errors.wrong: margin of error is always the same regardless of sample size
common_errors.correct: Margin of error decreases as sample size increases. Larger samples give more precise estimates with smaller margins of error.
